At his estate in Buzancy, near Soissons, the Marquis de Puységur tried the technique on a young farmworker, Victor Race, who was ill. rows.subject: Seventeen seconds. A much longer explanation.
rows.preheader_plan: NASA's Apollo 1 findings, and why a tidy explanation can mislead.
rows.approximate_unconfigured_55_word_excerpt: The surviving recording is precise about one thing. At 23:31:04.7 GMT on January 27, 1967, the first of Apollo 1's final two crew transmissions began. At 23:31:21.8, the second ended. Between those timestamps: 17.1 seconds. Seventeen seconds is an arresting headline. It is also a trap for anyone who mistakes a precise number for a
rows.proposed_custom_excerpt_NOT_APPLIED: The Apollo 204 Review Board logged 17.1 seconds between the first recorded crew report of fire and the end of the last transmission. That interval does not reveal the precise ignition instant or source. The record instead exposes interacting hazards: oxygen, combustible materials and an inward-opening hatch. Read The Hatch Opened Inward.
